cases.name: Linda Rowden
cases.about:
Her family's memorial Facebook page said, "Her family knew she was going to be a strong woman, one who left her mark wherever she went, when she started walking by 9 months.

Linda was adored by everyone she came in contact with throughout her short life. As a child, she led Chris and her 3 younger cousins, Eddie, Ricky and Bobby, on grand adventures in and around Perkiomen Valley; mischief never stopped her. One of Chris’s favorite childhood memories was Linda in the front yard of their grandparents' farmhouse leading the memorial procession of cousins across the lawn and up the hill for dead/injured creatures they discovered while playing.

Linda and Chris had a sisterly bond that no one could break. Linda loved seeing how far she could push buttons before Chris dove in and swooped her up like a sister would. In their teen years, Linda introduced her sister to one of her very best friends, Louie, and this year Chris and Lou will celebrate their 46th wedding anniversary!

Linda seemed to attract everyone to her and had a heart bigger than most. She found ways to love people who didn't love themselves. Linda cared for everyone and loved hard. She was the biggest cheerleader for the underdogs, making sure no-one was ever left behind without a friend. Jack always told stories about how Linda would bring home the homeless or those less fortunate than her for a delicious home-cooked meal in the comfort of her family home.

Linda had such a passionate and kind-hearted personality. Chris vividly remembers Linda becoming so upset about the mistreatment of elderly people in care that she walked away from 2 jobs when management dismissed her concerns. Linda was passionate about life and her family and friends. She was excelling in her career as a businesswoman in Norristown, building memories and living life as any woman in her mid-twenties should be doing."
cases.narrative: He was riding in the back seat and shot her in the neck and right side as she was driving her car.
